questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The units UWA offered and the possibility of living on my own. (No college dorms)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The orientation team at my uni sent out a lot of information (emails) before arrival, so I knew what to expect. I also got a uni-mentor, which is a student who will help you with any questions you might have throughout the semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had orientation week (the first week) and they had scheduled a lot of activities so felt like I got to meet people and see campus right away. However, you did not have to participate in everything, so it was totally fine to stay home or by yourself if that felt right. There was no pressure at all to participate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my off campus housing before I arrived. I would definitely recommend starting to look early because everything was booked when I arrived. There are a lot of international students in Perth, so start looking early to secure a place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of co-living accommodation in Perth CBD (central Perth) but rent can be expensive. You can also find a private housing accommodation. A lot of people rent a room in a house in the suburbs which is also cheaper. Remember to check your travel time to campus. Campus is located outside of CBD (approx. 20 min by bus), but there are free busses in the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not know that the university offered help with housing, so if you need help after your arrival please use them. They are great!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy. Again, there was a lot of information on the first day in Orientation week.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Orientation week gave you information about units, deadlines, schedules and other free services offered at campus.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: SESA and Exchange and Study Abroad advisers were there to help with any questions throughout the semester.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the units that I wanted from the beginning. My impression was, that everyone studying abroad got their preferred units.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask questions if there is anything you are unsure about. There is always someone available to help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything was fine and the teachers and professors were nice.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took level 1 units (BA 1. year) even though I was a 3. year student. The level were quite easy and there was a lot of introductory classes such as essay writing, referencing and such. But it was all right since UWA use a different reference style than UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Everything is different in terms of grades. They use marks in Australia and you are given marks throughout the semester that eventually will make up your final mark (your grade). You are given participation marks in most units which will be 10% of your final mark. The teaching is therefore very different since they take attendance and expect you to be prepared for every tutorial (class). Lectures are quite similar to UCPH but do not expect a lot of students to attend the lectures since that is the only time they do not take attendance. There was a lot of assignments throughout the semester which was not something I expected. But teachers are so nice and will help you with just about anything if you ask.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MGMT1135 Organisational Behaviour
MKTG1203 Introduction to Marketing
MGMT1136 Management and Organisations
COMM1002 Cultures, New Media and Communications

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
It really depends on what you are interested in and currently studying. 
I really enjoyed COMM1002 because it had a creative aspect where we got to work in Photoshop.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Fees when using my Danish creditcard. Be aware of this when you use your Danish creditcard. 
I opened an Australian bank account to avoid the fees, which is free and you can very easily transfer money from your Danish account to your Australian.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Uber rides are very cheap. And so is public transport. On your first day on Orientation week you can go to The Guild Village on campus and buy a Smartrider (Rejsekort). You will automatically get a student discount and cheaper fares in general throughout your stay.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not join any clubs during my stay, but there are a lot of different clubs available at UWA. There are also a lot of sports teams you can join.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All different clubs and social events. Music, sports, hobbies, specific interests such as Harry Potter, photography, religion, law, political clubs etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: UWA has a theme every week throughout the semster. One week is pride week, another week is sustainability week. There are tons of events on and off campus which is mostly free events and lots of opportunities to help out or join. Lots of talks, concerts and other events too.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Fremantle is located 30 min with train from Perth and has the best market on weekends. Also the beaches in Fremantle are amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very similar to the Danish culture. So very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you live with Australian students then you will know them and their friends. Australians are very laidback people and will take you anywhere (like their friends' parties). In my experience people will host parties or get togethers all the time. Also connecting with other international students are a great way to meet people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Don't think too much about who is buying what. Australians are likely to buy you a drink/beer/food without expecting you to pay them back. This is in my opinion very different to the Danish culture. Also get used to strange haircuts, people walking barefoot in the street and using Australian slang that you are not quite sure what means. Everyone is so friendly and happy, so just don't think too much.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The casual, laidback culture and everyone is asking you how you are doing ALL THE TIME :-)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don' spend too much time overthinking what you say and do (and not do). 
2. Use your studentcard for discounts at cafes, restaurants and stores 
3. Wear sunscreen everyday

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of events and social things going on at campus everyday. Don't stress yourself about attending everything. That is impossible. Remember to listen to yourself.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Completing a semester abroad. This has always been a dream of mine, and I feel very good about my decision.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living by myself in a new place. You spend a lot of time by yourself and that can be daunting at times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy your stay and remember to make it your own. Do what feels right and don't feel like you have to attend every party or social event if you are not up for it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
